hero.heading: Join a second machine without port forwarding.
hero.lead: Start with one node. Add another at home, at a relative's place or on a VPS, and manage them as one. Nodes find each other by key, not by IP address.

items.title: Join with a token
items.body: crust cast join with a one-time token. No IPs, no port forwarding.

items.title: Replicated state
items.body: The control plane state is replicated with Raft, so any node can answer.

items.title: Multi-site
items.body: Nodes in different homes connect over iroh, direct where possible, relayed where not.

items.title: Placement
items.body: Pin a workload to a node, a site or a label, or let Crustates choose.

items.title: Off-site backups
items.body: Back up to a node at another site with one policy.

items.title: Mixed hardware
items.body: A mini PC, a NAS box and a Raspberry Pi in one cluster, amd64 and arm64.

items.title: Rolling upgrades
items.body: Molt upgrades one node at a time and keeps quorum.

items.title: One console
items.body: Every node, VM and app in the same console, CLI and API.

items.title: Live migration
items.body: Move a running VM between nodes. Later.

how.heading: Small clusters, done right.
how.lead: Cast is built for 1 to a handful of nodes, not a data centre. It stays simple until you need more.

steps.title: Start single
steps.body: One node keeps its state in SQLite. No cluster overhead.

steps.title: Add a node
steps.body: The second node joins by token; state moves to Raft with openraft.

steps.title: Connect sites
steps.body: iroh finds a path between homes; WireGuard carries node traffic.

ask.body: "Which node has room for another Windows VM?" The assistant looks at capacity across nodes and suggests where to place it.
ask.command: crust ask "which node has room for a 8 GiB VM?"

faq.title: Do I need three nodes?
faq.body: No. One node works fine. Three give automatic failover; two work with a small witness.

faq.title: Do nodes need to be on the same network?
faq.body: No. iroh connects them across sites without port forwarding.

faq.title: Is this Kubernetes?
faq.body: No. The API is Kubernetes-shaped, but there is no Kubernetes underneath.

faq.title: Can I mix a Pi with a PC?
faq.body: Yes. Workloads are placed on nodes that match their architecture.
